content.text: Associated w/ rapid maternal weight gain & growth of the uterus
Dizygotic (fraternal): due to fertilization of 2 ova by 2 separate sperm (66%)
Increasing maternal age and increasing parity are independent RF’s for dizygotic twinning, and rates are higher among mothers of families with twins
Placental membrane composed of two layers: amnion (nearest the fetus) & chorion (outer layer) – together form the amniotic sac
*can have 2 amnions w/ 1 chorion, but not 2 chorions w/ 1 amnion
Conjoined Twins: division is incomplete, most common fusion being the chest and/or abdomen
Preterm labor, spontaneous abortion, preeclampsia, anemia
*MCC of morbidity is preterm labor & delivery
Twins are delivered at an average of 35 weeks, triplets at 32 weeks, and quadruplets 30 weeks
Intrauterine growth restriction, placental abnormalities, breech presentation, umbilical cord prolapse, preeclampsia
Twin-Twin Transfusion Syndrome: as development of a monochorionic gestation progresses, various vascular anastomoses between the fetuses can develop & can lead to TTTS
Net flow from one twin to another
